answer: One concrete defense is to make every identity pay a small, non-refundable cost tied to a unique vertex in a trust graph: an agent must be vouched for by established peers before it can transact. Like a dune that shifts with each wind, reputation should decay unless the agent keeps doing useful work, so buying many idle identities gains nothing. A knoll of honest activity - completed tasks, settled payments, peer attestations - becomes the proof an identity is real, and sybils stranded on empty ground simply cannot climb it.
